hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain).
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to the room.
Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.5 is moderate, roughly u in 0.3-0.6.
Step response has lag with time constant of tens of seconds and needs >100 s to settle.
There is no large dead zone: even u=0.1 produces a measurable rise versus u=0.
Steady-state y versus u is approximately linear up to the soft limit, without strong saturation.
Sensor noise is small, short-term variation <0.01 peak-to-peak.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Direction, magnitude of gain and lag/time-to-settle, which determine required steady input and controller speed; a mid-level long hold best separates these competing unknowns.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case rise 0.0508 + 0.006*0.5*180 = 0.591 stays below soft limit 0.85 with ~0.26 margin, assuming no decay or lag.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.05 toward 0.3-0.5 with decreasing slope and no overshoot; end slope still >0 if not yet settled.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero experiments completed, minimum three required; gain, lag, u=0 decay, linearity, dead zone and noise are all unresolved so a controller cannot be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: holding half power for 3 minutes to measure heating direction, size and speed.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Zero-input decay behavior and cooling time constant/ambient (H2, H4), which determines whether output falls on its own, how fast a controller can cool without overshoot, and anchors the low end of the gain curve for linearity.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is current y 0.4967 + 0.006*0.0*180 = 0.4967, well below soft limit 0.85; with u=0 no heating can occur, only passive cooling.
proposal.expected_observation: If H2/H4 are right, y decays monotonically from ~0.50 toward 0.15-0.25 over 180 s with diminishing negative slope and no undershoot below ~0.05; end slope still negative because cooling needs >180 s to fully settle.
proposal.readiness_justification: Heating gain direction, holding input ~0.5, heating settling time, and noise are resolved from E1+E2, but only 2 experiments completed so readiness requires a third; cooling decay rate, symmetry of time constant, and linearity/second amplitude remain unmeasured and are needed for controller integral and overshoot handling, so not yet ready.
proposal.operator_note: Holding at 0.5 reached ~0.49 near target, next stepping power to zero for 180s to measure cooldown and ambient.

proposal.expected_observation: If linear-gain hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.19 toward ~0.58 with decreasing slope, reaching ~0.45-0.55 after 180 s with end slope still >0 and no overshoot, clearly above the E1 trajectory at same elapsed time; if strongly saturating, it will flatten early below ~0.45.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, settling time ~300 s, zero-input decay, holding input ~0.5, and low noise are resolved by E1-E3, but linearity/local gain rests on a single steady point at u=0.5 and dead zone is untested, so a controller cannot yet be safely tuned without one second-amplitude test.
proposal.operator_note: Hold heater at 60% for three minutes from current cool state to measure upper gain and check linearity.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound with no decay or lag: 0.5343 + 0.006*0.4*120 = 0.8223, which stays below soft limit 0.85.

One small step-down near target is needed to fix bias before controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping down slightly to 0.4 to check holding power after unexpected continued rise at 0.5.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain).
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to the room.
Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.5 is ~0.44-0.47 (~0.45); steady-state for u=0.5 is ~0.54-0.57 and overshoots target.
Step response has lag with time constant ~130-170 s and needs ~250-320 s total to settle.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state holding input for target 0.5 (H3) and local gain, which sets controller bias and prevents systematic offset or overshoot; a direct hold at estimated u* from near-target separates incomplete settling from gain error after E2 vs E5 conflict.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound with no decay or lag is current y 0.4913 + 0.006*0.45*120 = 0.8153, which stays below soft limit 0.85.
proposal.expected_observation: If leading hypotheses are right (ss(u)=~0.05+1.0*u, tau~150s, u*=~0.45), y starting ~0.491 will stay nearly flat near target, drifting only to ~0.48-0.51 with small negative or near-zero slope (-0.0006 to +0.0002) and no overshoot; if true u* is <=0.40, y will rise toward >0.52, if >=0.50 y will fall toward <0.47, cleanly separating holding-error.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, decay, lag (~150s), linearity, and noise are well resolved from E1-E6, but steady-state holding input is not: E2 suggested ss(0.5)~0.49 while E5 rose to 0.534 and E6 decay at 0.4 implies ss(0.5)~0.55, so u* is uncertain by ~0.05 which directly sets controller bias and overshoot; one bounded hold at the estimated u* is needed before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: Holding near target at 0.45 for 2 minutes to pin the steady-state input that holds 0.5.
